messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: SLO alert: streaming p99 latency spike in us-east-1 for model:redwood-compat-v3 after precision-profile rollout (int8-calib-v2). Threshold breached (p99 > 800ms). Paging oncall. Investigate and post updates.

Ben (oncall): on it. hopping into metrics now. any customer-facing 5xxs?

Carla (ml-infra): seeing a sharp rise in KV-cache miss ratio and dequant spill logs correlated with the spike window. cal profile applied at ~5876501200 yesterday.

Ben (oncall): customers A and C reported intermittent streaming stalls + dropped fragments, some 504s. ETA to reproduce locally?

Carla (ml-infra): repro is flaky. running a tail capture on a small canary of traffic -> attached log snippet:

```
[2026-02-23T04:12:01Z] model: redwood-compat-v3 precision:int8-calib-v2 token_batch:1 latency_ms:1020 kv_miss:true kv_load_ms:320 dequant_warn: true
[2026-02-23T04:12:01Z] streaming: stall_detected seq:120 stall_duration_ms:900
```

Carla (ml-infra): also seeing increased CPU on dequant worker threads, and some backend RPC timeouts to kv-cache nodes. p95 moved from ~80ms to ~250ms, p99 to ~1.1s.

Aisha (sre): thanks. can we toggle fallback to fp16 for the affected model/route? need quick mitigation to reduce customer impact.

Carla (ml-infra): yes, we have a fallback slot. recommending: immediate policy switch to fp16-fallback, disable int8-calib-v2 rollout, and drain canaries.

Ben (oncall): do it. @DeployBot, apply routing fallback for route: /v1/stream/redwood-compat-v3 -> precision=fallback-fp16, scope=us-east-1, reason="paging - precision spike"

DeployBot: command queued:
```
revert_precision_profile --model redwood-compat-v3 --from int8-calib-v2 --to fp16-fallback --region us-east-1 --reason "paging - precision spike"
```

DeployBot: rollback triggered, 3 nodes targeted, expected rollforward time ~45s. I'll post status updates. :gear:

Diego (product): note: affected customers are on streaming tier. please confirm if any data-path changes needed for their clients when precision changes.

Carla (ml-infra): no client-visible API change; only model execution precision. output tokens remain same shape. streaming framing unchanged.

Aisha (sre): monitoring dashboards -> start a diff on p95/p99, stream stall count, kv-cache error rate, and tail CPU. tagging CS for customer comms. @Ben keep oncall lead.

Ben (oncall): got it. running live tail + heap snapshot on one affected node. provisioning a temporary dedicated node pool and routing 20% traffic to it as a mitigation experiment.

Carla (ml-infra): FYI metrics after rollback begin: p99 dropped from ~1.1s -> ~210ms within 90s for most routes. stream stall count halved. KV-miss rate improving.

IncidentBot: update: rollback completed at 5876550180. Auto-alert suppressed while p99 < 800ms sustained for 5m.

Diego (product): good. need postmortem: how did int8-calib-v2 pass tests but cause KV-cache pressure and dequant thrash? might be a calibration edge-case with long-context chat workloads.

Carla (ml-infra): hypothesis: the calibration produced denser KV usage and smaller quant chunks causing more frequent dequant ops per request -> increased contention under long contexts. logs show higher per-token dequant CPU. planning a deeper trace and calibration re-run with larger representative prompt sets.

Aisha (sre): action items: 1) Carla to run an expanded calibration benchmark with long-context traces and patch calibrator to emit KV-usage profile. 2) Ben to keep temporary route in place until we have a safe int8 profile + QA signoff. 3) Diego to coordinate customer comms for impacted streaming tenants. 4) SRE to add a telemetry alarm for dequant CPU/kv-miss correlation.

Carla (ml-infra): copying planned PR: calibrator: add "kv_usage_histogram" output + threshold gating. will open PR and tag owners.

Ben (oncall): leaving follow-up notes in oncall doc. if we see another spike, escalate to infra lead and consider temporarily restricting long-context to fp16.

Diego (product): approve comms draft, will rerun with legal for wording.

IncidentBot: final update: incident status -> mitigated (rollback + routing experiment). severity: Sev3 -> monitoring. thread closed for now, follow-ups tracked in #postmortems (link) and PR-3245. :white_check_mark:

Aisha (sre): thanks team. we'll reconvene for 1-hour postmortem and assign owners.

Carla (ml-infra): FYI I'll include synthetic replay results + calibration snapshot in the PM.

Ben (oncall): done for now, leaving handoff notes for next oncall.

[end of thread]
